finding.claim: The unauthenticated POST /hooks/test endpoint passes the request body field `callback` straight to axios.post. An attacker can make the server send a POST to any host, scheme or port, including internal services and cloud metadata. The response status is returned to the caller, so the attacker can use it to probe internal hosts and ports. Axios follows redirects by default, so a redirect from an attacker-controlled host also reaches internal targets.
finding.source: req.body.callback (POST /hooks/test JSON body, attacker-controlled, no authentication)

trace.note: `pub` router is the public router, with no auth middleware applied
The value is passed unmodified as the URL to axios.post
The upstream status code is returned to the caller (oracle for internal port and host scanning)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist or blocklist, no DNS resolution check, and no URL parsing. No redirect restriction (axios follows up to 5 redirects by default). requireAdmin is applied only to the `admin` router (routes.js:12), not to `pub`. I did not see the router mounted because only routes.js exists, so any middleware applied at mount time is unknown.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post and returns r.status, on the `pub` router (routes.js:4) that has no auth; requireAdmin is only on `admin` (routes.js:12), and routes.js is the only file, so mount-time middleware could not be checked.

finding.claim: GET /diagnostics/fetch passes the query parameter `url` directly to axios.get with no destination validation. A caller who passes the admin check can make the server request internal hosts or cloud metadata (for example http://169.254.169.254/...), follow redirects, and read back the response status. This is lower severity than SSRF-1 because it is limited to admin sessions. It is still a candidate where admins are less trusted than the host network, for example tenant admins in a multi-tenant deployment, or when session.role can be influenced.
finding.source: req.query.url (GET /diagnostics/fetch query string; reachable only with req.session.role === 'admin')

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates all routes on the admin router
req.query.url is passed unmodified to axios.get
The upstream status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the admin role check (authorization, not destination validation). There is no scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP or metadata blocklist, no DNS pinning, and no redirect limit. How the session role is set, and whether `admin` is mounted, is not visible in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: none for destination; only the admin role check (routes.js:8, applied via admin.use at routes.js:12)
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate, but req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after requireAdmin (routes.js:8, 12) passes, so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control it, and nothing in this directory sets session.role to suggest it can be influenced.
